sets.t: Subarachnoid Haemorrhage and Intracranial Aneurysms: MCQs

qs.q: A 54-year-old woman is admitted to the neurosurgical intensive care unit following a ruptured cerebral aneurysm. Her mean arterial pressure is 145 mmHg and systolic blood pressure is 175 mmHg. Which of the following is the most appropriate agent to initiate for acute blood pressure control?
qs.e: Labetalol is a titratable agent with a short half-life that controls blood pressure without increasing intracranial pressure. Nitrates should be avoided because they raise intracranial pressure.
qs.s: Subarachnoid Haemorrhage and Intracranial Aneurysms: MCQs

qs.q: A 50-year-old woman is recovering well after endovascular coiling of a cerebral aneurysm. She has no focal neurological deficits. Which of the following long-term screening recommendations applies to her family members?
o: Routine annual screening for all siblings regardless of family history
No screening is ever indicated for family members of patients with sporadic aneurysms
Screening of first-degree relatives in families with two or more affected members
Genetic testing of all children once they reach eighteen years of age
qs.e: Screening is recommended for first-degree relatives specifically in families with two or more affected members. Risk factor control such as stopping smoking and treating hypertension also matters.
